Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15171 of 2022
Applicant :- Subhash Gautam

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Uma Nath Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.
Vakalatnam filed by Mrs. Anjali Singh, Advocate on behalf of the applicant today is taken on record.

Heard Mrs. Anjali Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ravi Prakash Bhatt, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the entire record.

The instant second application for bail has been moved on behalf of the applicant, Subhash Gautam with the prayer to enlarge him on bail in F.I.R./Case Crime No.847 of 2019, under Section 498A,
304B, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Police Station Kotwali City, District Bulandshahar during pendency of the trial.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant came to be falsely implicated in this case because he happens to be husband of the deceased, who died an unnatural death in the house of the present applicant accidentally.
Her further submission is that neither the applicant demanded any dowry nor he treated the deceased with cruelty, who died accidentally due septicemia caused by burn injuries.
Some witnesses of fact, namely, Indrapal and Praveen have not supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile.
The accused/applicant is languishing in jail since 04.10.2019, who has no previous criminal history.

sentences.text: His further submission is that in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and he will also fully cooperate with the trial court in getting the trial concluded expeditiously.
He has also submitted that the applicant will not intimidate or pressurize the witnesses or any other persons acquainted with the facts of the present case.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail by submitting that the trial is still underway.
The deceased died due to septicemia caused by ante-mortem burn injuries.

His further submission is that the deceased has made an unequivocal and specific reliable dying declaration in which she has made a specific allegation against her husband, the present applicant, who is stated to have set her ablaze.

Having heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of the record, it transpires that a first information report came to be lodged against the named six accused persons including the present applicant.
There is a specific allegation against the applicant regarding demand of dowry and treating the deceased with cruelty due to non-fulfillment of demand of dowry.
The deceased has admittedly made a dying declaration wherein she has stated that the present applicant set her ablaze by pouring kerosene oil.

The cause of death of the deceased,
according to post-mortem report, is reported to be septicemia due to ante-mortem burn injuries which corroborates the manner of commission of offence as stated by the deceased in her dying declaration.
There is nothing on record to show that the deceased was not in a medically fit condition to make such dying declaration or such dying declaration was tutored.

Thus, having regard to the aforesaid overall facts and circumstances of this case and also keeping in view the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, nature and manner of commission of offence and evidence regarding the complicity of applicant, no case for bail, at this stage, is made out.
Accordingly, the instant second application for bail is rejected.

However, keeping in view the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 04.10.2019, the learned trial Court concerned is directed to get the trial concluded with utmost expedition, without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the parties, preferably within a period of one year from the date of production of certified copy/computerized copy of this order, in case there is no other legal impediment.
It is made clear that the trial of the aforesaid case shall be conducted without being influenced by any observation made herein above which are confined to the disposal of the instant second application for bail.
S.S.P./S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned are directed to ensure that witnesses are present on the date fixed so that their testimonies may be recorded without there being any hindrance.
Office is directed to communicate this order to S.S.P./S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned as well as trial Court concerned separately for its necessary compliance through Subhash Gautam vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39800616/
2 E-mail/Fax, forthwith.
